description:
Remove the legacy bare-short-id destination from container archive resolution, so a container archives into its marker-backed directory or its preferred directory and nothing else, and state the rule in the adopter reference.

## Background

- `resolve_container_destination` (`crates/jit/src/domain/artifact_classifier.rs:415-485`) takes `legacy_root` (the bare `<archive_root>/<short-id>` directory from `artifact_destination_root`, `:1608-1613`), derives the archive root as its parent (`:421-424`), and falls back to it when no child carries a matching `.jit-container` marker and the legacy directory exists (`:474-482`). `ArtifactEvidenceError::MissingArchiveRoot` (`:406-407`) exists only for that parent derivation.
- The one destination-evidence function in `crates/jit/src/commands/archive.rs` captures the legacy root as evidence for this fallback, and `capture_archive_plan` computes `legacy` from `artifact_destination_root` (`archive.rs:540`).
- `classify_artifacts` (`artifact_classifier.rs:662`) falls back to `artifact_destination_root` when the inventory carries no destination root (`:667-670`); the archive planner always sets one through `with_destination_root`, but the domain discovery builds its inventory without one (`ArtifactClassificationInventory::new` in `discover_archive_artifacts`, `crates/jit/src/domain/artifact_discovery.rs:473`), and the discovery tests classify such inventories directly. Its other callers are `crates/jit/src/commands/archive.rs:302, 826`, the classifier unit tests, and the citation-test helper `plan_with_scan` (`crates/jit/src/storage/artifact_planning.rs:501-532`, call at `:530`), which `archive-preview-through-execute-planner` relocates into `crates/jit/src/storage/artifact_inspection.rs`.
- Tests: `test_destination_resolution_uses_marker_freeze_legacy_fallback_and_duplicate_evidence` (`artifact_classifier.rs:2380`) and `test_resolve_container_destination_adopts_a_preexisting_identifier_only_directory_without_relocating_it` (`:2440`) assert the fallback.
- Data check: the three bare short-id directories under this repository's `dev/archive/` each carry a matching `.jit-container`, so the marker branch already resolves them.
- `docs/reference/cli-commands.md:374-385` says planning resolves to an existing unsuffixed `<archive_root>/<container-short-id>/` directory when no marker matches (`:381-383`). `docs/reference/configuration.md:159` describes the bare short-id directory as the preferred name when no slug resolves; that remains true.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `resolve_container_destination` takes the archive root, the preferred root and the container id, and returns a marker-backed root, a conflict, or the preferred root; no parameter, evidence request or branch refers to a legacy short-id root.
- [hard] REQ-02: `classify_artifacts` takes the destination root as a required argument with no fallback derivation; the domain discovery, the relocated `plan_with_scan` helper and their tests pass it explicitly; `artifact_destination_root` serves only document targets or no longer exists.
- [hard] REQ-03: A domain test shows that an unmarked bare short-id directory under the archive root is not adopted: resolution returns the preferred root. It fails today, where the fallback returns the bare directory; the two fallback tests are replaced.
- [hard] REQ-04: The archive destination section of `docs/reference/cli-commands.md` states marker reuse and the preferred root only.

## Notes

- Behaviour change: a container whose bare short-id directory exists without a matching marker no longer archives into it; it archives into its preferred root, and an existing unmarked preferred directory is reported as today. Asserted by REQ-03's test. The adopter description of destination resolution changes in the docs (REQ-04).
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.
title: Archive destinations drop the short-id fallback
